landmarks.name: McLaughlin Library
facts: It is the main library, named after the founder of General Motors of Canada.

landmarks.name: Johnston Hall
facts: It is named after the founder and first principal of the Ontario Agricultural College.
It was built in 1931 as a student residence and home for administrative offices.

landmarks.name: Lambton Hall
facts: It is a co-ed residence in the north area of campus, home to over 380 students.

landmarks.name: Watson Hall
facts: It is the only women-only residence, home to 50 students.

landmarks.name: South Residence
facts: It is the largest residence on campus, home to about 1,800 students.

landmarks.name: Rozanski Hall
facts: Its lecture halls can hold more than 1,500 students at once.
Completed in 2003, it is named after a former university president, Mordechai ____.

landmarks.name: Summerlee Science Complex
facts: It was completed in 2007 with help from Ontario's SuperBuild program, for science teaching and research.

landmarks.name: Ontario Veterinary College
facts: It is one of Canada's oldest schools for animal doctors, with first classes in Toronto in 1862.
It moved to Guelph in 1922 and became a founding college of the University of Guelph in 1964.

landmarks.name: Centre for Biodiversity Genomics
facts: It is home to the International Barcode of Life project, which identifies species by DNA.
Founded in 2007 under another name, it took its current name in 2012 after its second stage was built.

landmarks.name: Macdonald Institute
facts: It was established in 1903 to house women's home economics and nature study programs.

landmarks.name: University Centre
facts: The campus radio station CFRU has broadcast from studios here since 1974.
A dispute over plans for it led the university to dissolve the student government, Union Council, in 1970.

landmarks.name: War Memorial Hall
facts: It is one of the buildings students reach by cutting across Johnston Green.

landmarks.name: Art Gallery of Guelph
facts: It was called the Macdonald Stewart Art Centre from 1978 to 2014.
Its collection started in 1926 when the Ontario Agricultural College bought Tom Thomson's painting The Drive.

landmarks.name: Creelman Hall
facts: It is one of the main dining halls on campus.

landmarks.name: Gryphon Field House
facts: It has an indoor 200 m track on artificial turf.

landmarks.name: Alumni Stadium
facts: It is home to the university's varsity football team.
It was built in 1970; an $18 million expansion and renovation was announced in 2011.
